entries.title: Bulk-remove reviewers and open assignments from an Awards round
entries.summary: Program managers can now remove several reviewers from an Awards round at once, by selecting them or by tag, and separately remove the open (unscored) assignments of the reviewers they pick on **Assign**. Reviewers who have already saved a score or declined a submission are kept and listed with the reason; other rounds are not affected. In **My Reviews**, reviewers no longer see an Interest Form review round where they have nothing assigned once assignments have gone out.

where.path: Awards → program → round → Reviewers (Remove by tag, Remove from round); Awards → program → round → Assign → Remove from these submissions

entries.use_case: When a reviewer is no longer available or was added to the wrong round, a program manager can remove them — and clear their unscored assignments — in one bulk action instead of one by one, without disturbing any work already submitted or other rounds.

cs_action.note: Nothing to turn on. The entry waits for both the API (web-api#5192) and the controls (web-ui-v2#1502) to reach production; the controls stay hidden until the API answers.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer has added reviewers to an Awards round in bulk and now needs to remove a group — e.g. a tag-based committee that changed.
internal.who_should_get_it: Awards add-on customers running multi-round programs with large reviewer panels.
internal.staff_path: Awards → program → round → Reviewers → Remove by tag / select rows → Remove from round
internal.gotchas: Reviewers with any saved score or decline in the round are kept and listed with a reason; they have to be removed individually. Only the selected round is affected; other rounds are untouched. Tags must belong to the program. On Assign, Remove is disabled while step 1 is set to By condition.
internal.talk_track: If you need to swap out a whole committee from a round, you can now remove them by tag or selection in one step — anyone who already scored something stays, and you see the full list before confirming.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should add a section explaining how to bulk-remove reviewers from an Awards round by selection or tag, including the dry-run preview, which reviewers are kept (those with saved scores or declines), and how to bulk-remove open assignments separately.
draft.why_use_it: Awards review rounds often involve large panels that shift as programs evolve. Bulk reviewer management lets you keep each round's roster accurate without manual one-by-one edits, and the dry-run preview shows exactly who will be removed and who will be kept before you commit. Reviewers who have already scored or declined a submission are always preserved, so no completed work is lost.

entries.title: Turn a session recording into a slide video
entries.summary: A session recording now becomes a **slide video** on its own: the audio cut to the speaker's own deck, each slide on screen while it is talked about, ready shortly after the transcript. Pick a layout, add an opening and closing title slide from the event's Slides designs, fix any slide's timing, or ask for changes in chat.

enable.path: Nothing to turn on: slide videos are on for every account, on the event under Marketing → Media

where.path: Marketing → Media on the event → a recording → Slide video

entries.use_case: Most sessions are recorded as audio or a room camera, but the deck is what people want to watch. Every talk with a deck becomes a shareable video for a gallery, an LMS or a feed the same day, without anyone sitting in a video editor.

cs_action.note: Made automatically once a recording's transcript is ready, if the recording is linked to its session and the session has a PDF or PowerPoint deck in its files. On for every account; Open in Clips shows only where Clips is on.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer records sessions (especially audio only) and asks how to repurpose them, or asks for slides synced to recordings for on-demand content or CE.
internal.who_should_get_it: Marketing customers who record sessions and collect speaker decks — conferences with on-demand libraries, associations publishing education content.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Media → open a recording → Slide video (on audio recordings: Actions → Slide video)
internal.gotchas: Needs the recording linked to its session and a deck in that session's files. A deck uploaded after the transcript does not start it automatically: open Slide video and click Make the slide video. Opening and closing cards are offered only for recordings that belong to an event. Start over from the deck discards edits.
internal.talk_track: Upload the recording and the speaker's slides; Sessionboard lines the slides up with what is said and gives you a branded video you can share or download, and you can adjust it in plain words.

entries.title: Choose which session roles can edit submissions in a portal
entries.summary: Under **Manage Related Submissions and Participants**, a portal now has **Roles That Can Edit**: only participants who hold one of the chosen session roles on a submission, for example the Speaker, can edit it, its participants or add people. Everyone else on that submission sees it read-only, and the check is made per submission.

enable.path: Portals → portal → Configuration → Manage Related Submissions and Participants → Roles That Can Edit

where.path: Speaker portal → session flyover (read-only for other roles)

entries.use_case: When co-presenters should see a submission but only the lead speaker should change it, the organizer picks that role once per portal instead of policing edits by hand.

cs_action.note: Requested by Messe München. Empty = unchanged behaviour, so nothing changes until a role is picked.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why panelists or co-authors can change the lead speaker's submission in the portal.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events using Manage Related Submissions and Participants with several roles per session (Messe München first).
internal.staff_path: Event → Portals → open the portal → Configuration → Manage Related Submissions and Participants → Roles That Can Edit
internal.gotchas: A submitter who holds none of the chosen roles on their own submission sees it read-only too. Sponsor and exhibitor accounts are not affected. Legacy speaker / chairperson / moderator rows count as the reserved role of the same name. The submission form opened by its own link is not covered by this filter.
internal.talk_track: Pick the roles that can edit in the portal settings, and everyone else on the submission sees it read-only — decided per session.

entries.title: Filter the Sessions Summary merge tag by session status
entries.summary: The **Sessions Summary** merge tag can now list only some statuses, for example `{{{sessions_summary:status=accepted}}}` for a confirmation email. Tick the statuses under **Only sessions with status** in the **Insert Sessions Summary** dialog, custom statuses included; the preview reflects the filter and existing tags keep listing every session.

where.path: Email editor → merge tags → Sessions Summary → Insert Sessions Summary dialog

entries.use_case: A speaker with an accepted and a declined submission gets a confirmation email that lists only the accepted one.

cs_action.note: Nothing to turn on. The status list appears in the dialog once the API is in production.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer sends acceptance or logistics emails from Contacts and the table shows declined or pending sessions too (ACU asked).
internal.who_should_get_it: Any event emailing speakers with a table of their sessions.
internal.staff_path: Event → Communications → compose → Merge tags → Sessions Summary → Only sessions with status
internal.gotchas: Picking a system status (Accepted) also includes custom statuses built on it; pick the custom status to be exact. A recipient with no matching session gets no table.
internal.talk_track: Tick Accepted in the Sessions Summary dialog and each speaker's table lists only their accepted sessions.

entries.title: Day, Week, Month and Rooms say when they are filtered
entries.summary: When a filter is applied on the agenda, **Day**, **Week**, **Month** and **Rooms** now show *Only showing sessions that match filters* above the calendar, with a **Clear** button that removes the calendar's filters.

where.path: Program → Agenda → Day / Week / Month / Rooms

entries.use_case: Schedulers no longer mistake a filtered calendar for missing sessions.

cs_action.note: On for everyone.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports sessions missing from the calendar views.
internal.who_should_get_it: Everyone who schedules on the agenda calendar.
internal.staff_path: Event → Program → Agenda → Day → apply a filter in Filters & Views
internal.gotchas: Clear removes the calendar's filters only; the List tab keeps its own.
internal.talk_track: If sessions look missing on the calendar, check the bar at the top — it says when a filter is on, and Clear shows everything again.

entries.title: Choose the modules and update types in release notes by email
entries.summary: Once **Release notes by email** is on, pick the **Modules** you work in and the **Update types** (New, Improved, Fixed) you want. The digest lists only matching updates, skips days with none, and an empty filter keeps sending everything.

where.path: Community → What's New → Release notes by email; Account settings → Community notifications

entries.use_case: Team members get only the updates relevant to their work instead of skipping the whole email.

cs_action.note: Tahaluf asked for this; let them know the filters exist.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer says the release-notes email is too much to read.
internal.who_should_get_it: Admins subscribed to release notes by email, especially large teams split by module.
internal.staff_path: Community → What's New → Release notes by email card (filters appear once switched on)
internal.gotchas: Filters are per email address, not per organization. Updates with no type never pass a type filter.
internal.talk_track: Tick only the modules and update types you care about, and the email lists just those.

entries.title: Flat-fee early-bird tiers that ignore pricing rules
entries.summary: Each Date & Time Tier now has a **Flat fee** switch, off by default. While a flat-fee tier is active, its price is what every entrant pays and pricing rules do not apply; promo codes and VAT still do. When it ends, pricing returns to the base fee or next tier plus rules. Works on Awards programs and submission form payments.

enable.path: Awards → program → Pricing → Date & Time Tiers → tier → Flat fee

where.path: Awards pricing step; submission form → Payments & Fees → Date & Time Tiers

entries.use_case: An early-bird price can be one number for everyone, with category pricing starting only after the window closes.

cs_action.note: ACU was promised Early Bird during the sale; this makes it usable with their category rules.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer wants one early-bird price for all categories.
internal.who_should_get_it: Awards and CFP customers with category pricing rules (ACU first).
internal.staff_path: Awards → program → Pricing → Date & Time Tiers → Flat fee switch on the tier
internal.gotchas: Promo codes and VAT still apply to a flat-fee tier. The switch only appears once the API is in production.
internal.talk_track: Turn on Flat fee on the Early bird tier and everyone pays that price until it ends; your category prices take over after.

entries.title: Session format on agenda embed cards
entries.summary: When **Format** is one of an agenda embed's Agenda fields, each card in the grid now shows the session's format as a tag next to its track, without opening the pop-up. Sessions with no format show no tag.

enable.path: Publish → Embeds → embed → Field Options → Agenda → Format

where.path: Agenda embed grid cards on the customer's website

entries.use_case: Attendees can tell a keynote from a workshop at a glance.

cs_action.note: Agenda embeds that already tick Format (it fed the pop-up) will show the tag once the embeds PROD publish runs — a manual release after merge.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks to show the format on the agenda grid (Messe München).
internal.who_should_get_it: Events publishing the Agenda embed.
internal.staff_path: Event → Publish → Embeds → open the embed → Field Options → Agenda → tick Format
internal.gotchas: Embeds deploy to production by a manual release, so the tag appears after that publish, not at merge.
internal.talk_track: Tick Format in the embed's Agenda fields and every card shows the session format next to the track.

entries.title: Built-in participant roles show in the reviewer's language
entries.summary: In the review portal, the participant roles every event starts with (**Speaker**, **Chairperson**, **Moderator**) and the **Primary** tag now appear in the reviewer's chosen language (Spanish, French or German) on submission cards, **Print all** and the submission page. Roles your team created or renamed keep their names.

where.path: Review portal → round → submission cards (participant chips); submission page → participants

entries.use_case: A Spanish-speaking reviewer reads participant roles in Spanish instead of English on every card.

cs_action.note: Built-in roles translate automatically. Custom role names such as Presenting author or Co-author: set each language's name in Event Settings → Roles (since 2026-11-09, entry translatable-participant-role-names). Field names and dropdown values need a Language variant with Show this variant checked in Fields.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A multilingual customer reports English text on reviewer cards in another language.
internal.who_should_get_it: Multilingual events using Review plans.
internal.staff_path: Site → My Reviews → Review language → Español → open a round
internal.gotchas: Without a name set per language in Event Settings → Roles, only the three built-in roles with their original names are translated. Track, Language and custom field labels and values come from Fields → Language variants.
internal.talk_track: Speaker, Chairperson and Moderator follow the reviewer's language automatically. For your field names and values, add a Spanish variant in Fields.

entries.title: Upload-slot reminders reach subsession speakers
entries.summary: Slot coverage, upload reminders, the overdue notice, a slot's **Who this reaches** count and the Coordinator's deadlines now include the speakers on subsessions, so the presenter of each poster or talk inside a parent block is reminded about their own file. Someone on both a parent session and one of its subsessions still gets one reminder per slot: about the parent session while its file is missing, then about the subsession if that file is still missing once the parent's is in.

where.path: Program → Submissions → Submission files → Slot coverage; Program Settings → Files → Upload slots → open a slot → Who this reaches

entries.use_case: Poster halls and symposia keep the real presenters on subsessions. Until now they could see an upload slot in their portal but were never reminded about it, so the organizer had to chase each poster by hand.

cs_action.note: Speakers on subsessions that still owe a dated slot start getting reminders from the first daily run after release. If a slot is already past due, they get its overdue notice on that first run. To keep subsessions out of a slot, set its Applies to to Top-level submissions only before the release.

internal.when_to_bring_up: With customers running poster halls, symposia or lightning rounds as parent sessions with subsessions and collecting files through upload slots.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with upload slots on and subsessions under parent sessions (medical and scientific poster sessions especially).
internal.staff_path: Program → Submissions → Submission files → Slot coverage (rows now include subsessions); open a slot → Who this reaches
internal.gotchas: A person on the parent and a subsession gets the parent's reminder while the parent still owes the file, and the subsession's only after the parent's file is in. Two subsessions of the same parent are two files and two reminders. The coverage API's include_subsessions=false still gives the parents-only view.
internal.talk_track: If your poster presenters are on subsessions, they now get the same upload reminders as everyone else, and nobody on both the block and a poster gets the same nudge twice.

entries.title: Connect your own domain to an Awards Site
entries.summary: Once Sessionboard turns on **Site Domains** for your organization, admins connect a domain such as `awards.yourassociation.org` to an Awards Site themselves: **Domains** on the Site overview opens **Settings > Domains**, which gives you the DNS records and serves the Site over HTTPS when they resolve.

enable.path: Ask your customer success manager to turn on Site Domains, then Settings > Domains > Site domain

where.path: Sites → Site overview → Domains; Settings → Domains → Site domain

entries.use_case: Associations want submitters to land on awards.theirdomain.org, not a Sessionboard address. Once Site Domains is on, their admin connects it without a support ticket.

cs_action.note: Turn on Site Domains in the organization's Admin Settings (staff only). For a Site that belongs to an event, turn on the event's Site Domains switch instead. The customer then connects the domain.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks to run their Awards Site on their own domain, or compares us to Evessio or OpenWater, which include it.
internal.who_should_get_it: Awards customers who want a branded address for their Site.
internal.staff_path: Organization → Settings → Admin Settings → Site Domains → Save
internal.gotchas: One domain per Site. Use a subdomain; a bare domain needs CNAME flattening at the DNS host. Records can take up to an hour to resolve. While the switch is off, staff see the Domains button with a lock and customers see nothing.
internal.talk_track: We turn on Site Domains for you, then your admin enters awards.yourdomain.org under Settings > Domains, sends the DNS records to IT, and the Site goes live on HTTPS as soon as they resolve.

entries.title: Session reports label the session ID column "Session ID"
entries.summary: In a module report built on sessions, and in the **Session N** blocks of people and group reports, the session's ID column is now headed **Session ID**. It used to be headed **Friendly ID**, which pushed the real Friendly ID field to a column with a long code after its name. Contact and group reports keep **Friendly ID**.

where.path: Reports → module report on Sessions → run or download

entries.use_case: Someone matching an exported session report against another system can tell the session ID and the Friendly ID apart by their headers.

cs_action.note: Nothing to do. Saved reports pick up the new header on their next run.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks why their session export had two Friendly ID columns, or a column header with a long code in it.
internal.who_should_get_it: Teams that export session reports into spreadsheets or other systems.
internal.staff_path: Reports → open a module report on Sessions → Run
internal.gotchas: A spreadsheet or import that matched on the old "Friendly ID" header for the session ID needs its column name updated to "Session ID".
internal.talk_track: Session exports now say Session ID for the session's ID, and Friendly ID only for the friendly ID.

entries.title: Title slides keep speakers' job titles and companies under long session titles
entries.summary: On a 16:9 title slide, a session title running to four lines used to squeeze the speaker grid until every speaker lost their **job title** and **company**. The speaker grid now keeps the height its rows need and the title shrinks to fit instead. Slides with shorter titles look the same as before.

where.path: Marketing → Slides → template → Generate slides

entries.use_case: A conference with long academic session titles gets title slides that still name each speaker's role and organization.

cs_action.note: Nothing to do. Regenerate any slides made before the fix to get the full speaker details.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports missing job titles or companies on generated title slides.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with long session titles that generate title slides.
internal.staff_path: Event → Marketing → Slides → pick a template → Generate slides
internal.gotchas: Slides generated before this fix are not changed until they are generated again.
internal.talk_track: Long titles now shrink to fit, so every speaker keeps their job title and company.

entries.title: Webinar share cards and emails link to the live registration page
entries.summary: Pre-webinar **share cards** linked to the event's short address, which fails when the event page's address is different (for example, a long event name or a custom domain). All six cards, the Dispatch call to action, recap and survey emails and webinar registration emails now use the same link as the webinar's **View page** button. **Regenerate** no longer times out while waiting for fonts.

where.path: Program → Webinars → webinar → Overview → Share cards

entries.use_case: Everyone who shares a pre-webinar card lands on a registration page that works.

cs_action.note: Cards made before the fix may carry the old link. Open the webinar's share cards and click Regenerate to refresh them.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says a webinar share card or QR code opens "Site could not be found".
internal.who_should_get_it: Teams promoting webinars with share cards, Advocacy or Dispatch.
internal.staff_path: Organization → Program → Webinars → open the webinar → Overview → Share cards → Show cards → Regenerate
internal.gotchas: Already-downloaded card images keep their old link; regenerate and re-share them.
internal.talk_track: Share cards, QR codes and webinar emails now point at the same live page as View page.

entries.title: Exhibitors and sponsors can join an Advocacy Groups campaign from its open link
entries.summary: Joining an Advocacy campaign for exhibitors and sponsors from its **open link** failed for everyone with an error. Joining now works, and the person lands on the campaign's **Share** tab without needing a portal.

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → exhibitor or sponsor campaign → Open link

entries.use_case: An organizer can post one link for all exhibitors and sponsors, and each one signs up and starts sharing.

cs_action.note: If a customer shared an open link before the fix, ask them to share it again; people who saw the error can now join.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that exhibitors could not sign up through an Advocacy open link.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events running Advocacy for exhibitors and sponsors.
internal.staff_path: Event → Marketing → Advocacy → open the campaign → Open link
internal.gotchas: Nothing changed for the attendee open link, which already worked.
internal.talk_track: The exhibitor and sponsor open link now signs people up straight into the campaign.

entries.title: A Field Rule pointing at a deleted Track, Format or Level no longer blocks saving
entries.summary: If an Assignment rule set a **Track**, **Format** or **Level** that was deleted after the rule was saved, every save that triggered the rule failed. Now Sessionboard skips that value, saves everything else, shows a warning, and logs **Not applied** with the reason in the **Rule Log**.

where.path: Organization Settings (or the event) → Library → Fields → Field Rules → rule's history icon (Rule Log)

entries.use_case: An event that tidies up its tracks or formats keeps saving sessions even if an old rule still names a removed value.

cs_action.note: Point the customer at the rule named in the warning and have them pick a value that still exists.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports session saves failing after they deleted a track, format or level.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events using Field Rules that assign catalog values.
internal.staff_path: Organization Settings → Library → Fields → Field Rules → open the rule's history icon (Rule Log); inside an event, Library → Fields → Field Rules
internal.gotchas: The rule itself is not changed; it keeps skipping the deleted value until someone edits it.
internal.talk_track: Saves go through now; the warning tells you which rule needs a new value.

entries.title: Swapcard field mappings load for an event without a saved connection
entries.summary: Opening **Swapcard** field mappings for an event that has no Swapcard connection of its own (it uses the organization's) failed with an error. The page now loads the organization's mappings.

where.path: Apps → Swapcard → Field mappings

entries.use_case: Teams mapping fields for Swapcard can open the mappings page on every event.

cs_action.note: Nothing to do.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports an error when opening Swapcard field mappings.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events syncing to Swapcard.
internal.staff_path: Event → Apps → Swapcard → Field mappings
internal.gotchas: None.
internal.talk_track: The Swapcard mappings page now opens on every event that uses the organization's connection.

entries.title: Connect domains once, then choose one per Site
entries.summary: Custom domains for Sites now live on one page. Connect a domain such as `events.yourassociation.org` once in **Settings > Domains**, for your organization or for an event, then choose it in any Site's **Domain** setting: Global and Awards Sites, Program Sites, Content Galleries, Learning Sites and event pages. A domain serves one Site at a time, and an event's Sites can use your organization's domains too.

enable.path: Ask your customer success manager to turn on Site Domains, then Settings > Domains > Site domain

where.path: Settings → Domains → Site domain; on each Site: Site overview → Domain (also the builder's Domain button, a Content Gallery's Domain tab, Learning Site settings, an event page's Where it lives)

entries.use_case: Customers with several Sites (an Awards Site, a Program Site, a gallery) connect their domains in one place and move a domain between Sites without a support ticket, for example from last year's Program Site to this year's.

cs_action.note: Turn on Site Domains in the organization's Admin Settings (staff only) so the organization can connect domains every Site can use. Turn on an event's Site Domains switch only if that event should connect domains of its own.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer wants their Sites on their own domain, or wants to move a domain to a new event's Site.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with a branded web address for their Awards Site, Program Site or galleries.
internal.staff_path: Organization → Settings → Admin Settings → Site Domains → Save (event: Event → Settings → Admin Settings → Site Domains)
internal.gotchas: A domain serves one Site at a time; picking one another Site uses moves it after a confirm. A domain connected from an event is listed on the organization page but only that event's Sites can use it. Deleting a Site keeps its domain connected. A pending domain can be chosen: the Site keeps its Sessionboard address until the domain is active.
internal.talk_track: Connect your domain once under Settings > Domains, send the DNS record to IT, then pick it on the Site. Next year, pick it on the new Site and the old one goes back to its Sessionboard address.

entries.title: Self-serve Marketing and Learning: field events, Pathways engagement scoring, Learning workspace, assistant approvals, and more
entries.summary: A large integration of self-serve capabilities across Marketing and Learning ships together. Key additions include: **Field Events** in Marketing (in-person events, tours, guest and plus-one management, gated invitation send, check-in, and results); **Pathways** engagement scoring with explainable scores, **Keep everyone engaged** rounds, owner pings, and Results bands; the **Sessionboard Learning** workspace (sign-up switch, Learning plans on self-serve billing, Credits, Meeting on demand, learner transcript PDF, Certifications in the Public API, and a paid meeting boost); **assistant approvals** so AI-generated sends, publishes, and spend require organizer sign-off under **Waiting for your OK**; and supporting additions including Slack and Microsoft Teams apps, Swapcard and Visit imports, a Brand section API, People add/import/export, and goal starters with suggested numbers.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Beta → Marketing, Learning, Pathways or Field Events → Request access; our team turns it on

where.path: Marketing → Field Events; Marketing → Pathways; Learning (org sidebar); Marketing → Goals; Marketing → People; Marketing → Brand

entries.use_case: Organizers who want to run in-person field events, score and nurture audience engagement automatically, and offer on-demand learning with CE credit — all from within Sessionboard — can now access these capabilities on self-serve billing without a custom contract. The assistant approval gate ensures AI-driven sends and spend are reviewed before they go out.

cs_action.note: Multiple migrations must run before the API deploys (see PR body for order). LEARNING_SIGNUP_ENABLED config flag and STRIPE_BILLING_PORTAL_CONFIG_LEARNING (sandbox only) must be set. Companion PRs in public-api, mcp-server, and web-ui-v2 must all be deployed in order: web-api → public-api → mcp-server → web-ui-v2.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks about running in-person field events, automating audience nurture, or adding CE credit and on-demand learning to their event program.
internal.who_should_get_it: Marketing beta customers and any org interested in Learning/CE credit; self-serve billing must be available in their region.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Field Events; Marketing → Pathways; Learning (org sidebar)
internal.gotchas: Stripe billing for Learning is sandbox-only at merge time — confirm production Stripe config before enabling for paying customers. Imported faculty from Cvent/Swoogo/Bizzabo have no disclosures yet, so those courses are held. Registration for field events is simple only — no large-event registration, onsite tooling, or live webinar tech. Credit writes go through the assistant approval rule.
internal.talk_track: You can now run a dinner or roadshow as a Field Event inside Marketing, automatically score every contact's engagement across webinars, emails, and sessions, and let attendees earn CE credit and download a transcript — all without leaving Sessionboard.

draft.docs_gap: The get-started guides for Marketing and Learning should be updated to cover: Field Events (in-person events, tours, guests, plus-ones, gated invitations, check-in, results); Pathways engagement scoring (explainable score, Keep everyone engaged rounds, owner pings, Results bands, engagement sources endpoint); the Learning workspace sign-up flow and self-serve billing; Meeting on demand (draft → review → publish); learner transcript PDF; Certifications in the Public API; paid meeting boost; assistant approval queue (Waiting for your OK, retry on failure); and the new People, Brand, and Goals (starters with suggested numbers) surfaces in Marketing.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard Marketing and Learning bring event promotion, audience engagement, and continuing education into one workspace. Marketing lets you run field events and webinars, score every contact's engagement across all your channels, and turn recordings into shareable content — without stitching together separate tools. Learning adds structured plans, credits, certifications, and learner transcripts so your audience can earn and prove credit directly from your event content.

entries.title: Set up and use the Learning workspace directly from the product
entries.summary: A new **Learning** workspace is now available inside the shared product frame, letting organizers set up courses, manage learners, award credits, and track engagement without leaving Sessionboard. Highlights include a **Learning Home** with an **Ask** assistant, a **Learners** person view, a **Credits** page, billing with a meeting boost, and an **Add Learning** card to get started from inside the product. Meetings imported from Cvent, Swoogo, or Bizzabo become draft courses automatically; imported faculty courses are held until disclosures are added.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Beta → Learning → Request access (our team turns it on); a new organization can also sign up at /signup/learning

where.path: Learning → Home / Learners / Credits / On Demand / Courses / Certifications / Results

entries.use_case: Organizations that run continuing education or professional development programs can now build and manage their entire learning operation — courses, learner records, credits, certifications, and engagement signals — inside Sessionboard, without a separate LMS. Teams importing events from Cvent, Swoogo, or Bizzabo get draft courses created automatically from those meetings.

cs_action.note: Learning is a Beta: our team turns it on from the Request access card. Self-serve sign-up at /signup/learning is behind LEARNING_SIGNUP_ENABLED. Needs web-api#5193 (migrations first) and public-api#207 in production.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks about CE credit, continuing education, post-event on-demand content, or replacing a standalone LMS.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizations running accredited programs, professional associations, or any customer who awards CE or CME credit and wants learner engagement data alongside their event data.
internal.staff_path: Learning → Home
internal.gotchas: Imported faculty courses from Cvent/Swoogo/Bizzabo are held (not published) until disclosures are completed. The cross-product switcher between Marketing and Learning is deferred to a future release. Requires web-api#5193 (with its migrations) in production first.
internal.talk_track: If you're awarding credit or running on-demand content after your events, Learning gives you a single place to manage courses, track who's engaged, and issue certificates — and if you're already importing from Cvent or Swoogo, your meetings become draft courses automatically.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should be expanded to cover the new self-serve Learning workspace setup flow (the LearningSetup wizard and Add Learning card), the Learning Home with Ask, the Learners person view, Credits page, billing with meeting boost, registration import from Cvent/Swoogo/Bizzabo creating draft courses, and how faculty disclosure holds work on imported courses.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard Learning brings course management, credit tracking, and learner engagement into the same platform where you already manage speakers, sessions, and events. You can award credit, track who is engaged, issue certificates, and connect learning activity to the Pathways engine — all without switching tools. The Ask assistant on the Learning Home helps you act on what needs attention, and the on-demand library lets learners keep learning after an event ends.

entries.title: Access Awards workspace data through the Public API
entries.summary: The Public API now exposes **/v1/awards/workspace** routes, secured with **read:awards** and **write:awards** scopes, so integrations can read and write Awards workspace data programmatically. Event-restricted API keys are blocked from these routes. Enterprise-only capabilities (a second review round, entry fees/payments, SSO, and a named CSM) return a **403 enterprise_only** error on self-serve plans.

where.path: Awards → workspace (via Public API /v1/awards/workspace)

entries.use_case: Teams that manage Awards data in external systems — such as a CRM, data warehouse, or custom dashboard — can now pull and push Awards workspace data through the Public API without manual exports. Enterprise customers get full access; self-serve customers get the same routes but receive a clear error when they request an Enterprise-only capability.

cs_action.note: Awards sign-up is behind the AWARDS_SIGNUP_ENABLED flag and Stripe sandbox products are not yet created, so Checkout is not live. API routes exist but the full self-serve sign-up flow is not complete.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When an Awards customer asks about integrating their program data with an external system, or when a developer asks whether Awards is available in the Public API.
internal.who_should_get_it: Awards add-on customers and Enterprise Awards customers who use the Public API or build custom integrations.
internal.staff_path: Settings → API Tokens (org level) → generate a token with read:awards or write:awards scope
internal.gotchas: Event-restricted API keys are refused on all /v1/awards/workspace routes. Enterprise-only features (second review round, payments, SSO, named CSM) return 403 enterprise_only on self-serve plans — not a plan-gate UI, a hard API error. Awards sign-up is not yet live (AWARDS_SIGNUP_ENABLED flag off; Stripe products not created).
internal.talk_track: If you're building a custom integration or want to pull Awards data into your data warehouse, the Public API now has dedicated Awards workspace endpoints — just generate an org-level token with the awards scopes and you're ready to go.

draft.docs_gap: The API tokens guide should add a section listing the read:awards and write:awards scopes, explain that event-restricted keys cannot access /v1/awards/workspace routes, and note which capabilities are Enterprise-only at the API level.
draft.why_use_it: The Sessionboard Public API lets you connect Awards to the rest of your technology stack. Use it to sync submission data into your CRM, trigger downstream workflows when a round closes, or build custom reporting on top of your Awards programs — all without logging into Sessionboard. Org-level API tokens with the read:awards or write:awards scope control exactly what each integration can access.

entries.title: Scheduler respects pinned sessions, enforces a 90-day event limit, and applies "Avoid Parallel Topics" correctly
entries.summary: The **Scheduler** agent now correctly holds pinned sessions in place — other sessions and speakers can no longer be placed into a pinned room and time slot. Events longer than 90 days are rejected with a clear error before a draft is generated. The **Avoid Parallel Topics** rule now has real data to work with: for orgs with taxonomy topics enabled, the solver reads each session's primary topic and avoids scheduling sessions with the same topic in parallel. Run statistics gain a `warnings` field and `topic_coverage` so organizers can see when topic data is sparse.

where.path: Sessions → Agenda → Drafts → Generate Schedule

entries.use_case: When an organizer has manually pinned keynotes or anchor sessions to specific rooms and times, the Scheduler now honours those placements instead of overwriting them. If the event spans more than 90 days, the organizer gets an immediate error rather than a stalled or corrupted draft run.

cs_action.note: All fixes are default-on. The topic rule requires the org to have the generate_topics Properties row; CS does not need to act unless a customer asks why topics are not being used.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that pinned sessions were being overwritten by the Scheduler, or that the Avoid Parallel Topics rule seemed to have no effect.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the Scheduler agent, especially those with pinned keynotes or taxonomy topics configured.
internal.staff_path: Sessions → Agenda → Drafts → Generate Schedule → run stats → warnings
internal.gotchas: The Avoid Parallel Topics rule only fires for orgs that have the feature--generate_topics Properties row. Events longer than 90 days now get a 400 error on POST generate-schedule — the one known affected production event (5881, 371 days) would have been blocked. Topic coverage warnings appear in run stats when fewer than 50% of sessions have a topic.
internal.talk_track: The Scheduler now locks pinned sessions in place before solving, so your keynotes and anchor sessions stay exactly where you put them. It also reads your taxonomy topics and avoids scheduling same-topic sessions head-to-head — and if topic data is thin, the run stats will tell you.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document: (1) how pinned sessions interact with the Scheduler — what "pinned" means, the warnings surfaced when a pin cannot be honoured (pinned_no_time, pinned_outside_grid, etc.), and how to read them in run stats; (2) the 90-day event length limit and the error returned when it is exceeded; (3) how the Avoid Parallel Topics rule uses taxonomy topics, the topics_enabled flag in setup, and the topic_coverage and topics_unavailable/low_topic_coverage warnings in run stats.
draft.why_use_it: The Scheduler agent builds a draft agenda by placing sessions into rooms and time slots automatically, balancing speaker conflicts, room capacity, and soft rules like topic diversity. It saves hours of manual grid work on large programs and gives organizers a starting point they can refine rather than a blank calendar. Pinned sessions let you lock high-priority sessions in place before the solver runs, and topic-aware scheduling reduces the chance that attendees have to choose between two sessions on the same subject at the same time.

entries.title: Learning and Awards workspaces get a full chat experience and tailored sign-up flows
entries.summary: The **Learning** and **Awards** workspaces now use the same chat-first interface as Marketing: a persistent **Ask** composer, a **Chats** panel with search, a **New chat** button, a pinned **Setup** thread, and a **Getting started** checklist on the home page. The rail gains a **Learn** tab on both products. Sign-up for each product is now a guided conversation — Learning asks about learners and existing courses before previewing a credit-first or certification-first experience; Awards asks who the program is for, what is being awarded, and when nominations close, then drafts a named program with those settings and marks setup complete.

where.path: Learning workspace → Ask / Chats; Awards workspace → Ask / Chats; /signup/learning; /signup/awards

entries.use_case: Organizations evaluating Learning or Awards can now sign up through a short conversation that captures their goals and immediately creates a configured starting point — a credit-oriented Learning workspace or a named Awards program with categories and a nominations deadline — so they reach value without manual setup steps.

cs_action.note: Awards chat saving depends on web-api#5200 reaching production; until then, answers display correctly but are not persisted. Confirm the API is deployed before demoing Awards chat to customers.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When onboarding a new Learning or Awards customer, or when an existing customer asks how to get started faster.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any org with the Learning (beta) or Awards add-on.
internal.staff_path: Learning workspace → Ask; Awards workspace → Ask; /signup/learning or /signup/awards for new sign-ups
internal.gotchas: Awards chat answers display on screen even before web-api#5200 is live, but saving fails silently — do not demo Awards chat persistence until the API PR is confirmed deployed. The Awards sign-up drafts a program named '<Org> Awards <year>' with the categories and date the user provided; if the draft API call fails, the user is offered Try again (all answers kept) or a direct link to the workspace. Announcing winners is intentionally not available through Ask — it points to the Winners page instead because it triggers emails.
internal.talk_track: Learning and Awards now open with the same chat experience as Marketing — you can ask what to do next, get a checklist, and the setup thread stays pinned so you always know where you left off. Signing up is a short conversation that ends with a ready-to-use program.

draft.docs_gap: The Learning get-started guide should document the new chat-first workspace: the Chats panel, New chat, pinned Setup thread, Getting started checklist, and the Learn tab on the rail. A parallel section is needed in the Awards getting-started guide covering the same chat interface plus the conversational sign-up flow that drafts the first program.
draft.why_use_it: The Learning and Awards workspaces use a conversational interface so you can ask questions, get contextual guidance, and take actions — like opening nominations or assigning reviews — without hunting through menus. Chats are saved and replayable, the Setup thread stays pinned until you are done, and the Getting started checklist on the home page keeps next steps visible as your program grows.

entries.title: Send reviewer and draft-nomination reminders from the Awards workspace, and preview announcements before sending
entries.summary: The Awards workspace **Ask** chat can now send two kinds of reminder emails: one to reviewers who have unfinished scorecards (linking them directly to the review portal) and one to submitters who started but never submitted a nomination (only while the program is open). Before any reminder or announcement goes out, **Ask** shows a preview card listing exactly who will receive the email, who will be skipped (including anyone reminded in the last 24 hours), and any blocking reason — so organizers can approve before anything is sent. A 24-hour per-person, per-audience rate limit prevents duplicate reminders.

where.path: Awards → program → Ask (workspace chat)

entries.use_case: When a review deadline is approaching, a program manager can ask the Awards workspace to remind only the reviewers who still have incomplete scorecards — or nudge submitters who left a draft unfinished — without manually hunting down who needs a nudge. The preview card shows the exact recipient list before anything is sent, so there are no surprises.

cs_action.note: This is the API half only. The ui-v2 chat actions that surface the remind and announce-preview cards to organizers are in a follow-on PR. Do not promote to customers until both halves are live.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When an Awards customer is running a review cycle and struggling to chase down reviewers or incomplete nominations manually.
internal.who_should_get_it: Awards add-on customers actively running review rounds or open nomination periods.
internal.staff_path: Awards → program → Ask chat
internal.gotchas: Reminder emails to reviewers are only sent when the relevant review round is currently open under the portal's window rule and in the org's timezone — if the round is closed, the request returns a 422 block. Draft reminders return 422 if the program is no longer open. The 24-hour rate limit is per person per audience (reviewers vs. drafts) per program. Sandbox addresses are silently skipped. The announce preview now also blocks if any submitted nomination lacks a complete scorecard (reviews_incomplete), matching the same gate on the Winners page.
internal.talk_track: Instead of manually tracking who hasn't finished their scorecard or submitted their draft, you can ask the Awards workspace to send targeted reminders in one step — it shows you exactly who will get the email and skips anyone who was already reminded in the last 24 hours, so you stay in control without over-emailing.

draft.docs_gap: The awards notifications guide should add a section explaining the workspace chat's remind actions: the two audiences (reviewers with incomplete scorecards, submitters with unfinished drafts), the 24-hour per-person rate limit, the preview card that shows recipients and skipped contacts before sending, and the blocking conditions (round not open, program closed, reviews incomplete for announcements).
draft.why_use_it: The Awards workspace chat lets program managers take action on their program — sending reminders, announcing winners, and checking progress — without leaving the Awards module or building email campaigns by hand. Reminders are targeted automatically: only people with outstanding work receive them, and a built-in rate limit ensures no one is emailed more than once per 24-hour window per audience. Preview cards show the full recipient list and any blocked reasons before you approve, keeping you in control of every send.

entries.title: Ask in Awards can announce winners and send reviewer and draft reminders
entries.summary: The **Ask** chat in the Awards workspace can now announce winners and send reminder emails to reviewers or people with unfinished nominations. Each action shows a preview card — how many people will receive which email, who will be skipped, and any blockers — and requires an explicit confirmation click before anything is sent. If some announcement emails fail, **Ask** offers a **Retry** option for only the failures, also gated behind a confirmation. Saved chats replay previews as fresh previews and never re-send.

where.path: Awards → program → Ask

entries.use_case: When a program manager is ready to notify winners or nudge reviewers who haven't finished scoring, they can type a plain-language request in Ask — such as "announce winners" or "remind reviewers" — review exactly who will receive an email, and confirm the send without leaving the Awards workspace.

cs_action.note: This is the UI half only; the full announce and reminder preview API (web-api#5201) must also be deployed. Until the API ships, announce previews fall back to program counts (safe, no send), and reminder previews show an unavailability message and send nothing. Confirm the API release is live before promoting this to customers.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When an Awards customer asks how to notify winners or chase reviewers faster, especially for programs with many reviewers or multi-program setups.
internal.who_should_get_it: Awards add-on customers who run multi-round programs and want to manage winner announcements and reviewer reminders without leaving the Ask interface.
internal.staff_path: Awards → program → Ask (type 'announce winners', 'remind reviewers', or 'nudge the drafts')
internal.gotchas: Sends are blocked and show a link to the relevant page when blockers exist (e.g. no_winners, reviews_incomplete, no_site, review_not_open, review_closed). Reviewers reminded in the last 24 hours are automatically skipped and shown in the preview. The API half (web-api#5201) must be deployed for full functionality; without it, announce falls back to a count-based preview and reminders show an unavailability message.
internal.talk_track: From Ask, you can type 'announce winners' and see exactly how many winners, finalists, and thank-you emails will go out — with a blocker message and a direct link if anything isn't ready — then confirm with a second click. The same flow works for reminding reviewers or nudging people who haven't finished their nominations.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should add a section explaining how to use Ask to announce winners and send reviewer or draft-nomination reminders, including the preview card, confirmation step, retry for failed sends, blocker messages, and how saved chats replay without re-sending.
draft.why_use_it: Ask in the Awards workspace lets program managers take action through conversation instead of navigating separate settings pages. You describe what you want — announcing winners, reminding reviewers, or nudging people with unfinished nominations — and Ask shows a precise preview of who will be emailed and why anyone will be skipped before you commit. The two-step confirmation means a single mistyped request can never trigger a mass send.

entries.title: Session statuses clone and import correctly, preserving order and custom-name display
entries.summary: Three bugs affecting session statuses and portal login links are fixed. When cloning an event, session **Statuses** now copy independently of the Sessions module tick, so status configurations are never silently dropped. When importing statuses from the library, the **Show Custom Name** flag and the original sort order are both preserved. A fourth fix ensures that portal **magic-link** login emails are sent from a verified sender domain, so login links reliably arrive in speakers' inboxes.

where.path: Program Settings → Statuses; Event clone wizard; Portal login

entries.use_case: Organizers who clone events or import session statuses from the library no longer need to manually re-enter status order or re-enable the Show Custom Name flag. Portal login links now reach speakers reliably even when the org's custom sender domain is not authenticated.

cs_action.note: Events cloned before this fix (e.g. event 7143 cloned from 6591 on 2026-10-23) had status order and show_custom_name corrupted and were fixed by hand. Any other recently cloned events that imported statuses from the library may need the same manual repair — check with the customer.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that cloned events are missing statuses, status order looks wrong, custom status names are not showing, or portal magic-link emails are not arriving.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any organizer who clones events, imports session statuses from the library, or uses a custom org sender domain for portal login emails.
internal.staff_path: Program Settings → Statuses; Event clone wizard
internal.gotchas: The portal magic-link fix falls back to the platform sender address when the event or org sender domain fails the verified-domain check — organizers using an unauthenticated custom sender domain will see emails come from the platform address until they authenticate their domain. The 403 fix on Add to Session (SB-11225) is a security hardening change; contacts outside the event's org will now get a 404 instead of being enrolled.
internal.talk_track: If you cloned an event recently and your session statuses look out of order or custom names are not showing, this fix addresses that. Also, if speakers on a portal were not receiving their login link emails, that delivery issue is now resolved.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should add a note under Statuses explaining that statuses clone as a standalone option (independent of the Sessions module checkbox) and that library imports preserve Show Custom Name and source order.

entries.title: Automation email step clarifies recipient list when "Send to session recipients" is off
entries.summary: When the **Send to the session recipients above** toggle is off in an Automation email step, the recipient category selector is now disabled and the summary reads **"Will send to: team members only"** instead of showing a misleading participant category requirement and label.

where.path: Automations → automation → Then → Send Email → Recipients

entries.use_case: When an organizer builds an automation that sends email only to internal team members — not to session participants — the step no longer incorrectly demands a participant role selection or shows a misleading "Will send to: Chairpersons" summary, making the configuration intent clear at a glance.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports confusion about the recipient summary or a validation error when trying to save an automation email step with the session-recipients toggle off.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Automations with email steps scoped to team members only.
internal.staff_path: Automations → automation → Then → Send Email → Recipients
internal.gotchas: The underlying send behaviour was already correct — the session's recipients were already skipped when the toggle was off. This fix is UI-only: the selector is now disabled and the summary label is accurate.
internal.talk_track: If you have an automation that emails only your internal team, the recipient panel now shows 'Will send to: team members only' and stops asking you to pick a participant role — the step was already working correctly, it just looked wrong.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that when "Send to the session recipients above" is off, the participant category selector is disabled and the summary reads "Will send to: team members only".
draft.why_use_it: Automations let you trigger emails based on session or contact activity without manual follow-up. The email step's recipient controls let you target session participants, internal team members, or both, so the right people hear about changes at the right time.

entries.title: Awards pricing rules now flag questions that no longer exist on the form
entries.summary: On the **Pricing** setup step, any conditional fee rule that references a question deleted from the submission form now shows **"Question no longer on the form"** instead of a raw question ID. A banner counts how many rules can never affect the fee, and any answer option that has since been renamed is highlighted so organizers know the rule needs attention.

where.path: Awards → program → Setup wizard → Pricing

entries.use_case: When a submission form is rebuilt or questions are removed, pricing rules that referenced the old questions become silently inert. The new warnings let organizers immediately spot which rules are broken and fix or remove them before the program opens, so the fee calculator behaves as intended.

cs_action.note: Any Awards customer whose program application form was recreated after 2026-10-30 may have broken pricing rules. The fee calculator already skips them silently, so no incorrect charges have been applied, but the rules should be reviewed and corrected.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports unexpected pricing behaviour or has recently rebuilt their Awards submission form.
internal.who_should_get_it: Awards add-on customers who use conditional pricing rules and have modified or recreated their submission form questions.
internal.staff_path: Awards → program → Setup wizard → Pricing
internal.gotchas: The broken-rule banner and 'Question no longer on the form' label are display-only warnings; the fee calculator already skips broken rules silently, so no incorrect fees were charged. Organizers must manually delete or remap the broken rules.
internal.talk_track: If you rebuilt your submission form and some pricing rules now reference questions that no longer exist, the Pricing step will flag them clearly so you know exactly which rules to fix before submissions open.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should add a note explaining that pricing rules referencing deleted or recreated form questions are flagged with a warning banner on the Pricing step, and that those rules must be deleted or remapped to restore correct fee calculation.
draft.why_use_it: Conditional pricing rules let you charge different fees based on a submitter's answers — for example, a higher fee for a specific category or submission type. Clear warnings on stale rules mean you can trust that every rule in the list is actually wired to a live question and will fire correctly at checkout.

entries.title: Poster gallery voting, slot filters, narration duration and file placement corrected
entries.summary: Four bugs in the poster gallery and portal narration flow are resolved. **Vote eligibility** now correctly respects a gallery hall's content filters, so votes cast on posters outside the hall's allowed track are rejected instead of accepted. **Slot-fed gallery halls** now apply the slot's own session scope and filters consistently across the hall, preview, coverage and vote eligibility — fixing a mismatch where Coverage showed "1 of 1" while the hall showed 6 posters. **Slot coverage** now counts subsessions by default, so posters assigned via a slot to subsessions appear in coverage totals. **Narration uploads** are measured server-side with ffprobe/ffmpeg rather than trusting the browser's reported duration, a 5-second grace window is allowed, and the poster slot's deadline is enforced before any file is uploaded; a narration recorded at 300.75 s is no longer rejected. **Narration files** now appear on the correct poster slot card in the Files tab instead of under "Other files".

where.path: Program → Poster Gallery → gallery hall; Portal → poster card → Files / Narration

entries.use_case: Events using filtered poster halls with public voting can now trust that votes are only accepted for posters actually in the hall. Speakers uploading narrations near the time limit will no longer hit false rejections, and their narration file will appear in the right place on their poster card.

cs_action.note: Four separate bug fixes shipped together. Any customer who reported incorrect vote counts, wrong coverage numbers on slot-fed galleries, narration upload rejections near the 300 s limit, or narrations appearing under 'Other files' should be followed up with to confirm the fix resolves their issue.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that votes are being accepted outside a gallery's track filter, that slot-fed gallery coverage numbers don't match the hall, that narration uploads fail near the time limit, or that narration files land under 'Other files'.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Poster Gallery with content-filtered halls, slot-fed galleries, public voting, or portal narration.
internal.staff_path: Program → Poster Gallery → hall (vote eligibility); portal poster card → Files tab (narration placement); admin slot coverage + CSV (subsession counts)
internal.gotchas: Slot coverage now includes subsessions by default; pass include_subsessions=false to the coverage API to restore the old behaviour. Narration duration is now measured server-side — a 5 s grace window is allowed, and the stored length is capped at 300 s. The client-reported duration is only used as a fallback where no decoder is available.
internal.talk_track: We fixed four QA-caught bugs in poster galleries: votes now respect hall filters, slot-fed halls and coverage agree on poster counts, narrations near the 5-minute limit upload cleanly, and narration files show up on the right poster card.

draft.docs_gap: The poster gallery guide should document how content filters on a hall restrict vote eligibility, how slot-fed galleries apply session scope across the hall and coverage, and how narration duration is measured and enforced server-side including the 5-second grace window.

entries.title: Poster Gallery content preview, grouping, narration and view-as fixes
entries.summary: Several issues in the Poster Gallery builder and speaker portal are resolved. The **Content** tab now shows a live preview count ("N posters would match once you save") and a matching grid as you adjust content filters, before saving. Subsession posters are correctly grouped under their parent session block when **Group subsessions by parent** is on. **Open poster** and studio back-links now preserve the **View portal as** preview so admins are not redirected into editing a speaker's poster. Recording duration is clamped to the recorder's limit and the recording control is read-only when a slot is closed to uploads. Narration files are listed under their poster's slot on the admin **Files** tab and in the portal, and the studio no longer accepts a narration for a poster.

where.path: Program → Poster Gallery → Gallery builder (Content tab, header); public hall; speaker portal Files tab; poster studio; Sessions → session → Files tab

entries.use_case: Organizers building a poster gallery can now see exactly how many posters will appear before saving content filter changes, and subsession posters land in the right parent-session group. Speakers and admins previewing a portal as another user stay in that preview context when opening a poster or the studio.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that the poster gallery content count looked wrong before saving, subsession posters appeared in the wrong group, the view-as preview broke when opening a poster, or narration files were missing or misplaced on the Files tab.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any event using the Poster Gallery beta with subsessions, narrations, or the view-as admin preview.
internal.staff_path: Program → Poster Gallery → gallery → builder → Content tab
internal.gotchas: The live preview is debounced and only fires when content filters differ from the saved state; layout-only changes (group_subsessions_by_parent) do not trigger a preview request. Recording is read-only on the slot card and in the studio whenever the slot refuses uploads (deadline, session or event switch); max_files alone does not make it read-only.
internal.talk_track: The gallery builder now shows you a live count and grid of matching posters as you tweak content filters — no need to save and check. Subsession posters also land under the right parent block, and narration files are properly attributed to their poster's slot.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should add a section explaining the live content-filter preview in the gallery builder (the debounced "N posters would match" header and grid), how subsession grouping works under Session layout, and how narration files appear on the admin Files tab relative to their poster's slot.
